//: Two rules, both enforcing things DESIGN.md already states and nothing checked.
The Token Rule — 'a literal hex value in a stylesheet is a defect'. order-details.css held 26 of
them and passed every gate for months. src/styles/ is exempt because that is where a colour is
allowed to be a colour: the three theme files are the only place a token is assigned a value.
Logical properties — marketing.css had 16 physical direction declarations and auth.css 7, so the
two surfaces a visitor sees first were the two that did not mirror in Arabic. Every console
feature was already clean; this is what keeps it that way.
Only genuinely direction-dependent properties are listed. `width` and `height` read the same in
both directions, so banning them in favour of `inline-size`/`block-size` would have produced 180
findings that fix nothing — a rule that noisy gets switched off rather than obeyed.
Spacing — DESIGN.md's Token Rule covers 'every colour, radius, shadow and type step', and
spacing was the one scale never brought under it. theme.css now carries the six steps the
console actually measures on, named for the job each does. Two rules, because stylelint has no
baseline and one rule cannot say both things:
error   — a raw literal that IS one of the six steps. Every one of those has a token now, so
typing the number again is by definition a regression. This is the half that has to
hold: the debt regrew once already after being consolidated by hand.
warning — any other raw rem in a spacing property. 682 of these remain, off the scale
(0.6rem ×82, 0.85rem ×75, 0.35rem ×73, 0.7rem ×56 ...). Snapping them to the nearest
step moves at most 1.6px each, but it moves it on every screen and cannot be proved
safe the way the on-scale sweep was — so they are a backlog, not a broken build. An
error here would be the 180-finding rule the note above warns about.
`lint:css` passes --quiet so the gate shows errors only; `npm run lint:css:debt` prints the
warnings when someone is working the backlog down. Warnings nobody can see past are the same as
no rule at all.
Both leading-zero forms are matched: `.5rem` and `0.5rem` are the same measurement typed two
ways and the codebase held both.
